text: 8. When 19th-century European explorers encountered the towering curved walls and dry-stone towers of this African site, they hallucinated origins involving the Phoenicians or the Queen of Sheba, refusing to credit the local population. It wasn't until the archaeological work of Randall-MacIver and Gertrude Caton-Thompson that the site was rightfully attributed to the ancestors of the Shona people. These precise, mortar-less structures served as the royal palace for a kingdom that flourished between the 11th and 15th centuries. What is the name of this archaeological complex?
